messages:
Alana: Anyone seeing a correlation between the ephemeral wearcheck runs and GPU attach failures in us-west2?
Jonah: Yep — saw 3 attach failures around 18:12 UTC, nodes stuck in PROVISIONING for ~40s.
Sophie: Confirmed. p99 write_lat jumped to ~120ms, overall IOPS for /dev/nvme0n1 hit ~350k for ~90s. Batch allocation queue depth climbed noticeably.
Miguel: That matches the janitor schedule — wearcheck cron at 18:11 does scrub+trim across hot pools. Concurrency currently 16.
Alana: Oof. We throttle scrubs but hotsets are getting hammered. Anyone have a quick mitigation?
Jonah: Short term: reduce janitor concurrency to 4 and run with ionice (-c2 -n7) for scrub workers on canary pool. Also add random jitter to start times.
Sophie: I have a PR with those changes + per-pool rate limiter: PR #4123. It also moves heavy trim ops to low-priority IO. Example log: `wearcheck: starting scrub, concurrency=16, pool=ephemeral-us-west2-hotspot` then `ioctl: discard range: 1.2G`
Alana: Great. What's the rollback if that makes things worse?
Miguel: Rollback = revert PR and redeploy via deploy-bot. Fallback policy: route GPU attaches to dedicated reserva-pool in eu-west1 for the short window (will incur cross-region cost).
infra-bot: ALERT 18:12:24 - wearcheck-run triggered on pool=ephemeral-uswest2-hotspot; scrub_concurrency=16; sample_iops=349000; write_p99=118ms
Jonah: Can we change the attach scheduler to prefer nodes with low `scrub_score`? Soft-drain nodes that are being scrubbed instead of hard reserves.
Sophie: Added a `scrub_score` metric to console and a quick dashboard. Dashboard link (placeholder): https://console/redwood/dashboards/scrub-score
Alana: Note on cost: if we route attaches to eu-west1 for bursts expect ~+$0.7k/month at current traffic. Ops budget ok?
Miguel: Long term: propose moving checkpoint writer lanes to a small journaling SSD per host, or add an in-runtime write-coalescer to reduce small write amplification. Pitched in issue #102.
Sophie: Rolling the canary now: `kubectl -n infra patch cronjob/janitor-wearcheck -p '{"spec":{"concurrencyPolicy":"Forbid","suspend":false}}'` — be careful with quoting in the shell.
deploy-bot: Deploy started: PR #4123 -> canary pool us-west2-canary (build 2026-03-20T18:22:10Z)
Alana: :thumbsup: Monitor p99 write_lat, total IOPS, and gpu_attach_success over next 30m. Post any anomalies here.
Jonah: If attach failures keep happening we'll throttle checkpointers on submit with `--write-rate-limit` as an emergency measure.
Sophie: Adding a short-term alert: `scrub_iops_p99 > 200k AND gpu_attach_failures > 1` -> Pager.
Miguel: Pushed a tiny helper: `scripts/hotset_detect.sh` that marks nodes with >75% scrub_io for 5m and tags them.
Alana: Thanks all. Tagging @oncall for night watch and please paste graphs if anything trends.
Jonah: will do — if canary looks stable we'll roll to the rest of us-west2 with concurrency=3 and per-pool limiter.
Sophie: FYI I'll follow up with a short runbook: minimal steps to throttle scrubs, fallback routing, and rollback notes.
Miguel: And I'll open the hardware follow-up to track which models show worse wear amplification; might inform procurement.
Alana: Closing the loop later, keep updates here.
